title: Headless editor can segfault in WorkerThread when quitting after a clean project import
body:
# Headless editor can segfault in WorkerThread when quitting after a clean project import

### Tested versions

- Reproducible in Godot 4.7.2.stable.official [ed1daf0bf] (official Linux x86_64 binary).
- Earlier versions have not been tested.

### System information

Omarchy/Arch Linux, x86_64; Linux 7.2.3-arch1-3 at the time of the crashes; glibc 2.44+r24+g16be1518495f-1; Intel Core Ultra 5 228V; headless editor mode.

### Issue description

The headless editor intermittently crashes while performing a clean-cache project import and immediately quitting:

```
godot --headless --editor --path /tmp/a-line-import-check.XXXXXX --quit
```

systemd-coredump recorded at least eight SIGSEGV occurrences from repeated clean-import checks on 2026-09-18. Every sampled SIGSEGV used the same command pattern, and all eight crashing worker threads stopped at the same instruction address in the official stripped binary:

```
Signal: SIGSEGV
si_code: SEGV_MAPERR (one occurrence was SEGV_ACCERR)
crashing thread: WorkerThread 0
godot + 0x455c8b1
```

For one representative core:

```
Thread 1 (WorkerThread 0):
#0  0x000000000495c8b1 in ?? ()
#1  0x0000000004dd0f7e in ?? ()
#2  0x00000000045e9576 in ?? ()
#3  0x000000000458651e in ?? ()
#4  0x00000000020228f2 in ?? ()
#5  0x0000000001e6b93e in ?? ()
#6  0x0000000001e6e1fa in ?? ()
#7  0x0000000004904c4d in ?? ()
#8  0x000000000490535c in ?? ()
#9  0x0000000004406195 in ?? ()
#10 0x00000000052e6c23 in ?? ()
```

At the same time, the main thread was in `free()`:

```
#0  free () from /usr/lib/libc.so.6
#1  0x00000000004ba1b5 in ?? ()
#2  0x0000000001e983b8 in ?? ()
#3  0x0000000001e154ee in ?? ()
#4  0x0000000001e94f6b in ?? ()
```

The faulting instruction and registers were:

```
rip = 0x495c8b1
rdx = 0xbe522000
=> cmp %r14,(%r10,%rdx,8)
fault address = 0x7a953a917fd0
```

This looks consistent with editor teardown racing outstanding import worker activity, but that is an inference; the official binary is stripped and has no build ID, so the Godot frames could not be symbolized with Arch debuginfod.

Available memory was healthy (about 12 GiB available, swap unused), and there were no OOM-killer events. The project has no GDExtensions, C++ modules, or editor plugins.

Expected behavior: the editor should finish or cancel outstanding import work and exit normally when `--quit` is supplied, without a worker thread accessing released state.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start with a Godot project containing scripts, scenes, and imported WAV assets.
2. Copy it to a fresh temporary directory, excluding `.godot`.
3. Give the run isolated XDG data/config/cache directories.
4. Run:
   ```bash
   XDG_DATA_HOME="$TMP/xdg-data" \
   XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$TMP/xdg-config" \
   XDG_CACHE_HOME="$TMP/xdg-cache" \
   godot --headless --editor --path "$TMP" --quit
   ```
5. Repeat clean-cache runs. Some complete normally; others crash in the same worker-thread instruction.

A retry after deleting the temporary `.godot` and XDG directories typically succeeds, so timing appears relevant.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

A minimal standalone project has not yet been isolated. The failure was observed repeatedly during clean imports of a larger GDScript project. The consistent command, worker-thread address, and concurrent main-thread `free()` stack are included above in case they are sufficient to identify the shutdown path.
